content: The provided text appears to be a list of references formatted in a fragmented and non-standard way. 1. Hemoglobin concentrations are critical for diagnosing anemia and assessing its severity. The World Health Organization (WHO) provides guidelines and resources for this purpose, accessible via their official platforms. 2. Nutritional anemias have been extensively studied, with a WHO scientific group publishing a comprehensive report on their causes, prevention, and management. 3. De Maeyer EM, Dallman P, Gurney JM, Hallberg L, Sood SK, and Srikantia SG authored a guide for health administrators and program managers on preventing and controlling iron deficiency anemia through primary healthcare strategies. 4. The management of nutrition during major emergencies has been addressed in a WHO publication, offering guidance on maintaining nutritional health in crisis situations. 5. The United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF), United Nations University, and WHO collaborated on a guide for program managers to assess, prevent, and control iron deficiency anemia. 6. The WHO and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) released the second edition of a resource for assessing the iron status of populations, providing updated methodologies and recommendations. 7. Braat S, Fielding K, Han J, Jackson VE, Zaloumis S, Xu JXH, et al. conducted a study to establish hemoglobin thresholds for defining anemia across age groups from 6 months to 65 years, using international data sources. Their findings were published in The Lancet Haematology in 2024. 8. Sachdev HS, Porwal A, Acharya R, Ashraf S, Ramesh S, Khan N, et al. analyzed hemoglobin thresholds to define anemia in a national sample of healthy children and adolescents aged 1–19 years in India. This population-based study was published in The Lancet Global Health in 2021. 9. Addo OY, Yu EX, Williams AM, Young MF, Sharma AJ, Mei Z, et al. evaluated hemoglobin cutoff levels to define anemia among healthy individuals, with their findings published in JAMA Network Open in 2021. 10. Ohuma EO, Young MF, Martorell R, Ismail LC, Peña-Rosas JP, Purwar M, et al. investigated international hemoglobin distribution values in healthy pregnant women, publishing their results in EClinicalMedicine in 2020. 11. Ohuma EO, Jabin N, Young MF, Epie T, Martorell R, Peña-Rosas JP, et al. explored the association between maternal hemoglobin concentrations and maternal and neonatal outcomes in the INTERBIO-21st fetal study, published in The Lancet Haematology in 2023. 12. Villar J, Altman DG, Purwar M, Noble JA, Knight HE, Ruyan P, et al., as part of the International Fetal and Newborn Growth Consortium for the 21st Century, detailed the objectives, design, and implementation of the INTERGROWTH-21st Project in BJOG in 2013. 13. Kennedy SH, Victora CG, Craik R, Ash S, Barros FC, Barrosio HC, et al. conducted deep clinical and biological phenotyping of preterm birth and small-for-gestational-age syndromes in the INTERBIO-21st newborn case-control study, published in Gates Open Research in 2019. 14. Ali SA, Tikmani SS, Saleem S, Patel AB, Hibberd PL, Goudar SS, et al. examined hemoglobin concentrations and adverse birth outcomes in South Asian pregnant women, with findings published in Reproductive Health in 2020. 15. Jung J, Rahman MM, Rahman MS, Swe KT, Islam MR, Rahman MO, et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the effects of hemoglobin levels during pregnancy on maternal and infant outcomes, published in Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences in 2019. 16. Young MF, Oaks BM, Tandon S, Martorell R, Dewey KG, Wendt AS, et al. reviewed maternal hemoglobin concentrations across pregnancy and their associations with maternal and child health outcomes, publishing their findings in Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences in 2019. 17. Young MF, Oaks BM, Rogers HP, Tandon S, Martorell R, Dewey KG, et al. updated a global systematic review and meta-analysis on maternal low and high hemoglobin concentrations and their associations with adverse maternal and infant health outcomes, published in BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth in 2023. 18. Sharma AJ, Addo OY, Mei Z, and Suchdev PS reexamined hemoglobin adjustments for defining anemia, focusing on altitude and smoking, with their findings published in Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences in 2019. 19. Kanu FA, Jefferds ME, Williams AM, Suchdev PS, and Sharma AJ verified proposed hemoglobin adjustments for elevation among school-aged children, with their study published in Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences in 2019. 20. The WHO's World Malaria Report 2021 highlights the relationship between anemia and malaria, emphasizing the need for integrated approaches to address both conditions. 21. White N reviewed the interplay between anemia and malaria, with findings published in Malaria Journal in 2018. 22. Wiciński M, Liczner G, Cadelski K, Kołnierzak T, Nowaczewska M, and Malinowski B explored the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges of anemia of chronic diseases in Nutrients in 2020. 23. Fraenkel PG provided a comprehensive review of anemia of inflammation in Medical Clinics of North America in 2017. 24. Weiss G, Ganz T, and Goodnough LT discussed the pathophysiology and clinical implications of anemia of inflammation in Blood in 2019. 25. Ganz T reviewed anemia of inflammation in The New England Journal of Medicine in 2019, providing insights into its mechanisms and treatment strategies. 26. Gelaw Y, Getaneh Z, and Melku M conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on anemia as a risk factor for tuberculosis, published in Environmental Health and Preventive Medicine in 2021. 27. Chiossi G, Palomba S, Constantine MM, Falbo AI, Harirah HM, Saade GR, et al. established reference intervals for hemoglobin and hematocrit in low-risk pregnancy cohorts, highlighting racial differences, with findings published in Journal of Maternal-Fetal & Neonatal Medicine in 2019. 28. Varghese JS, Thomas T, and Kurpad AV evaluated hemoglobin cutoffs for mild anemia in Asians using data from national nutrition surveys, published in Indian Journal of Medical Research in 2019. 29. Lim E, Miyamura J, and Chen JJ compared racial and ethnic-specific reference intervals for common laboratory tests among Asians, Blacks, Hispanics, and Whites, with findings published in Hawaii Journal of Medicine & Public Health. 30. Weyand A and McGann P called for the elimination of race-based reference ranges in hematology, advocating for equitable practices in The Lancet Haematology in 2021. 31. Jallow MW, Cerami C, Clark TG, Prentice AM, and Campino S examined genetic variants associated with iron imbalance across global populations, with findings published in PLOS One in 2020. 32. Kang W, Barad A, Clark AG, Wang Y, Lin X, Gu Z, and O’Brien KO investigated ethnic differences in iron status, publishing their findings in Advances in Nutrition in 2021. 33. Karakochuk CD, Rappaport AI, Barr SI, and Green TJ compared mean hemoglobin concentrations in fasting venous and non-fasting capillary blood among Cambodian women, with findings published in Clinical Chemistry and Laboratory Medicine in 2017. 34. Larson LM, Braat S, Hasan MI, Mwangi MN, Estepa F, Hossain SJ, et al. analyzed pre-analytical and analytical factors affecting hemoglobin measurement and their impact on global anemia prevalence estimates, published in BMJ Global Health in 2021. 35. Neufeld L, Larson L, Kurpad A, Mburu S, Martorell R, and Brown K discussed the biological basis and policy implications of hemoglobin concentration and anemia diagnosis in venous and capillary blood, published in Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences in 2019. 36. Whitehead RD Jr., Zhang M, Sternberg MR, Schleicher RL, Drammeh B, Mapango C, et al. compared the effects of pre-analytical factors on hemoglobin measurement using two HemoCue® point-of-care analyzers, published in Clinical Biochemistry in 2017. 37. Da Silva Lopes K, Yamaji N, Rahman MO, Suto M, Takemoto Y, Garcia-Casal MN, et al. reviewed nutrition-specific interventions for preventing and controlling anemia throughout the life cycle, published in Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2021. 38. Kassebaum NJ and the GBD 2013 Anemia Collaborators assessed the global burden of anemia, publishing their findings in Hematology/Oncology Clinics of North America in 2016. 39. The GBD 2016 Disease and Injury Incidence and Prevalence Collaborators conducted a systematic analysis of global, regional, and national incidence, prevalence, and years lived with disability for 328 diseases and injuries, published in The Lancet in 2017. 40. Safiri S, Kolahi AA, Noori M, Nejadghaderi SA, Karamzad N, Bragazzi N, et al. analyzed the burden of anemia and its underlying causes in 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2019, published in Journal of Hematology & Oncology in 2021. 41. Horton S, Gelband H, Jamison D, Levin C, Nugent R, and Watkins D ranked 93 health interventions for lowand middle-income countries by cost-effectiveness, published in PLOS One in 2017. 42. The WHO provides a comprehensive framework for accelerating anemia reduction, accessible through their official resources. 43. The WHO's e-Library of Evidence for Nutrition Actions (eLENA) offers an online database of evidence-based interventions for addressing anemia and other nutritional challenges. 44. The WHO's handbook for guideline development outlines systematic approaches for creating evidence-based health recommendations. 45. The GRADE Working Group has developed frameworks for rating the quality of evidence and strength of recommendations, widely used in clinical practice guideline development. 46. The WHO's International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP) provides a centralized database for clinical trial information, promoting transparency and accessibility. 47. The WHO's Health Equity Assessment Toolkit enables the evaluation of health inequalities, with a focus on lowand middle-income countries. 48. The WHO's Global Database on the Implementation of Nutrition Action (GINA) tracks progress in implementing nutrition-related interventions worldwide. 49. The WHO's Global Targets Tracking Tool monitors progress toward achieving global health and nutrition targets. 50. The WHO's Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health and Ageing Data Portal provides comprehensive data on health outcomes across the life course.
